backfillRows.why: AoN innovation-1 (the REMASTER Armor innovation page; the record's aonParentId still points at the legacy innovation-5) prints "You gain resistance equal to 3 + half your level to void damage, or to vitality damage if you have void healing (such as if you're a dhampir)." The shipped row rode the void branch alone and carried the vitality half as PROSE on `condition`, so a dhampir inventor read a void resistance that never applies and had no vitality one, and the wg-values comparer saw a SET-GAP (theirs=vitality, ours=void,spirit,unholy,holy). The branch reader was built this batch and had no user: `whenVoidHealing` is declared at src/rules/types.ts:527 and gated in deriveDefenses at src/rules/derive.ts:2726 (resistances) / :2754 (weaknesses), over the same `negativeHealing` fact that function already computes at :2688. Entry 0 splits into the two mutually exclusive entries the gate exists for and the prose `condition` is dropped, because the branch now says what the sentence said. Whole-field re-emission of `resistances`; entries 1-3 of the superseded row are carried byte-identical.

findings.note: One field (`resistances`), one row, superseding the existing effect-backfill row for classFeatures/otherworldly-protection.resistances. Closes the wg-values SET-GAP on our side alone — wg-values already reads the resistance set, so no comparer teach is needed and none is authored. Tested on a BUILT living inventor (void, no vitality) and on a BUILT dhampir inventor (vitality, no void) through deriveDefenses.

CHECKED WHILE RE-EMITTING, no change: the shipped entries are already right and the premise that they key on the DAMAGING creature is refuted. `whenCreatureTrait` is documented at src/rules/types.ts:507 as "the entry belongs only to a character who HAS this creature trait" and is read at src/rules/derive.ts:2720 as hasCreatureTrait(c, db, ...) — the CHARACTER's own traits, through creatureTraitsOf. A sanctified character IS the one who holds the holy/unholy creature trait: build.ts:6289-6296 pushes it from the deity's `sanctification` answer for a cleric (one-option deities included) and build.ts:6331-6347 from a feat option's `grantsCreatureTraits` (the Cleric and Champion dedications, which is exactly the route innovation-1's "such as by also being a champion or cleric dedicated to a deity" names). So {type:'unholy', whenCreatureTrait:'holy'} already means "resist unholy damage if you are sanctified holy", which is print. No `whenSanctified` field is added — there is no reader for one, and the carrier that exists is correct.

backfillRows.why: AoN mystery-20, Cursebound 4: "You take a -10-foot status penalty to all your Speeds as your limbs begin to crumble like ash." The shipped row's speed modifier carries no `detail`, and modeMatches (src/rules/modes.ts:135) defaults a detail-less speed modifier to 'land' — the ruling deriveSpeeds has always applied, because the mode editor's plain "+10 to Speed" means the Speed you walk at. So the penalty hit the walking Speed and nothing else, while print and WG (SPEED / SPEED_FLY / SPEED_CLIMB / SPEED_BURROW / SPEED_SWIM) take all five. `detail: 'all'` is the carrier modes.ts:135 and deriveSpeeds' movement loop (src/rules/derive.ts:5246-5250) were built to read and that nothing shipped uses. Whole-field re-emission of `modifiers`; the -2 circumstance ranged-attack entry is carried byte-identical.

findings.note: The ROW HALF of the instruments group's VALUES line; the gate line itself is owned by `instruments`. One field (`modifiers`), one row, superseding the existing effect-backfill row for modes/curse-of-creeping-ashes-4.modifiers. The sibling `note` row on the same record needs no change — it already reads "a -10-foot status penalty to all your Speeds". Tested on a BUILT oracle given a fly Speed, through deriveSpeeds (and the raw modeNumberBonus match) with the SHIPPED mode record, not a hand-built one.
